notes: Deliberately not lowered again: the floors have already been rebased once for CI, and ratcheting a quality bar down to meet runner noise is how a perf gate stops meaning anything.
Deliberately not given --retries: a retry hides which of the two causes fired, while re-measuring inside the test keeps the failure meaningful.
riskClosures.correction: The first fix (best of three windows) was necessary but not sufficient, and the diagnosis was incomplete. CI still read 24.15 against the floor of 25. The real cause is that this branch CHANGED THE METRIC: main reads __MEXE__.fps, Phaser's lifetime average, after a 3s settle; the branch reads a 2s rAF window. The CI floors of 25/15 were calibrated for the lifetime average, so nightly's 5/5 pass on main and this branch's ~24 are not comparable numbers. A like-for-like local measurement (same machine, same single-window probe) found no regression: branch 60.8/60.5/42.7 versus main 57/56/56.

The test counted two turns and assumed the second was the guest's; on a slower runner the guest was still rendering the previous frame when the helper sampled it, so the host took both turns and no frame was ever dropped.
